title: 6515--Humidifier Heater Base Sources Sought
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE. The NCO 12, Great Lakes Acquisition Center, 115 S. 84th Street, Suite 101, Milwaukee, WI 53214, is performing market research to determine if there is a sufficient number of qualified: (1) Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); (2) Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB); or (3) Small or emerging small business firms, or (4) Other Than Small business firms, to provide Humidifier Heater base, Humidifier Sensor Cartridge, and Humidifier Expiratory Heater to the , Captain James A. Lovell Federal Health Care Center in North Chicago, IL. General Requirements: Brand Name or Equal The below products are known to meet the governments needs all equal parts will be considered. 950 Humidifier Heater base, 950 Humidifier Sensor Cartridge, and 950 Humidifier Expiratory Heater Wire Adapter or Equal Salient Characteristics: Therapy Profiles: Must support Invasive ventilation Must support Noninvasive ventilation Must support Nasal High Flow therapy. Temperature Probes: Must have no external temperature probes Must incorporate internal temperature probes that do not require special disinfection processing Circuit Compatibility: Must be compatible with single heated circuits for non-invasive ventilation. Must be compatible with double heated circuits for invasive ventilation. User Interface: Must have a simple user interface Must include touch screen monitors to create setting modifications Must allow mode changes Must allow comfort setting adjustments Must display and troubleshoot alarms Must provide access to Information and Service menus Alarms: Must have built-in alarms for various conditions including but not limited to: 1. High Temperature alarms 2. Low Temperature alarms 3. Water Out alarms 4. Circuit Disconnect alarms 5. Reverse Gas Flow alarms 6. System check alarms Compatibility: Must be compatible with all ventilation and gas flow delivery devices that is currently used at FHCC, Specifically, must be compatible with Medtronic 980 ventilators Specifically, must be compatible with Philips V60 BiPAP devices Specifically, must be compatible with Nihon Kohden 330, 440, and 550 ventilator systems All interested firms who can meet the requirements stated above should respond, in writing, INCLUDING ALL THE FOLLOWING: Company name. Address. Point of contact (name/title/telephone number/e-mail address). FSS / SEWP Contract number, if applicable. SAM Unique ID number. Tax ID number. Indication of which business category (SDVOSB, VOSB, Small Business or Other Than Small Business) for which the organization qualifies. A capability statement that addresses the organizations qualifications and ability to provide the requirement depicted above. Documentation from manufacturer (i.e. correspondence from manufacturer) of your firm being an authorized distributor for the manufacturer. Submit responses to the Contracting Specialist, Ryan Nugent, at Ryan.Nugent@va.gov no later than 8:00 AM (Central Standard Time), 23 November 2026. 36C25227Q0090 950 Humidifier Heaterbase shall be referenced on all correspondence regarding this announcement. TELEPHONIC INQUIRIES WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The NAICS Code 339112, Surgical and Medical Instrument Manufacturing, is applicable to this acquisition; the size standard is 1,000 employees. Interested firms are reminded that in accordance with FAR 4.12, prospective contractors shall complete electronic annual representations and certifications in conjunction with FAR 4.11 required registration in the Systems for Award Management (SAM) database prior to award of a contract. The Government will use responses to this notice to make an appropriate acquisition decision. This is the only notice; no other copies of this notice will be provided.

title: Hotel Lodging and Conference services in December 2026 in Sinaia/ Romania
description: The U.S. Government, through the issuing office, requests quotations from qualified hotel and conference service providers for accommodation, conference facilities, catering, audio-visual equipment, and technical support in connection with the DOJ OPDAT Workshop scheduled to take place in Sinaia, Romania. The contractor shall provide a comprehensive quotation addressing all requirements specified in this RFQ. he required services are as follows: Accommodation: Check-in December 7, 2026, and check-out December 11, 2026, for four (4) consecutive nights. Conference facilities, catering, and audio-visual support: December 8�10, 2026, covering three (3) workshop days. Hotel Accommodation The contractor shall provide: Thirty-four (34) single-occupancy rooms for four (4) consecutive nights, totaling 136 room-nights. Full breakfast included in the nightly room rate. Complimentary internet access for hotel guests. Suitable accommodation standards and amenities for official Government travelers. The quotation shall include: Name and address of the proposed hotel. Description of the hotel and proposed room category. Room amenities and available internet access. Confirmation of room availability for the requested dates. Nightly room rate per single-occupancy room. Applicable taxes and mandatory fees, itemized separately. Reservation, cancellation, no-show, and room-reduction policies. Room rates shall not exceed the applicable U.S. Government lodging per diem limit for the location and dates of stay. The contractor shall identify any additional charges that may apply, including early check-in, late check-out, parking, or other mandatory services. Conference Facilities The contractor shall provide one (1) dedicated conference room for three (3) consecutive days, December 8�10, 2026. The conference room shall accommodate a total of forty-three (43) participants, including five (5) presenters. The proposed seating arrangement shall provide a roundtable configuration for all participants, with the option to arrange a separate presidium table for the five (5) presenters, if required. The presenters are included in the total of 43 participants and shall not be considered additional attendees for catering or room-capacity purposes. The contractor shall: Describe the proposed conference room, including its dimensions and maximum seating capacity. Confirm that the room can accommodate the requested roundtable arrangement and optional separate presidium table. Identify any additional charges associated with the presidium setup. Describe available internet connectivity and technical capabilities. Confirm the availability of appropriate lighting, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning. Identify whether conference room setup, drinking water, stationery, and signage are included in the room rental or separately priced. Provide photographs or a floor plan of the proposed conference room, if available. Daily conference room access hours: Tuesday through Thursday, December 8�10, 2026 Daily hours: 09:00�17:00 Set-Up Access: Monday, December 7, 2026, from 13:00�18:00. Coffee Breaks The contractor shall provide two (2) coffee breaks per day for 43 participants, as follows: One (1) morning coffee break per day. One (1) afternoon coffee break per day. The services shall cover December 8�10, 2026, for a total of: 129 morning coffee breaks (43 participants � 3 days). 129 afternoon coffee breaks (43 participants � 3 days). The quotation shall include: Proposed morning and afternoon coffee break menus. (Includes snacks and juices. offerings shall vary daily) Selection of hot and cold beverages. Coffee, tea, drinking water, and appropriate refreshments. Food quantities and service arrangements. Any applicable service charges. Coffee Break Area: A separate area outside but adjacent to the main meeting room is preferred. D. Lunches The contractor shall provide one (1) buffet lunch per day for 43 participants on December 8�10, 2026, for a total of 129 meals. Lunch shall be provided in the hotel restaurant with seating for the full group- Buffet-style service is preferred The quotation shall include: Proposed buffet lunch menus for all three days. Selection of main courses, side dishes, salads, and desserts. Included beverages. Confirmation that vegetarian and other dietary requirements can be accommodated. Procedures for accommodating food allergies and special dietary restrictions. Any applicable service charges. The contractor shall specify the deadline for receiving final attendance numbers and dietary requirements. 3.5 Audio-Visual Equipment and Technical Support The contractor shall provide appropriate audio-visual equipment and on-site technical support throughout all three workshop days. description: Kaavan tuotantojärjestelmän hankinta Kaupunkiympäristön toimiala (KYMP) on toteuttamassa Kaavan tuotantojärjestelmän hankintaa. Helsingin kaupunkiympäristön toimiala hankkii kaavan tuotantojärjestelmän, jolla pystyy tuottamaan kansallisen kaavatietomallin mukaista asema- ja yleiskaavaa ja toimittamaan ne Suomen ympäristökeskuksen ylläpitämään rakennetun ympäristön tietojärjestelmään viimeistään vuoden 2029 alusta alkaen. Hankinta sisältää ohjelmistopalvelun käyttöoikeudet, ylläpidon ja tuen sekä kiinteähintaisen käyttöönottoprojektin. title: APN - BASE JANITORIAL SERVICES CFB SHILO, MANITOBA
description: Advance Procurement Notice BASE JANITORIAL SERVICES CFB SHILO, MANITOBA (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Shilo, Shilo Manitoba. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services The Department of National Defence and Defence Construction Canada intends to put in place a contract to provide all labour, material, supervision and equipment to supply janitorial services at CFB Shilo, Manitoba.  In general, the work includes, but not limited to: Janitorial cleaning services (internal and external elements) General Requirements wipe down benches, exercise equipment and weight machines; dusting of blinds; vacuuming of curtains and drapery; cleaning/stocking of dispensers; clean & disinfect door handles, handrails and switch plates cleaning and disinfecting of drinking fountains; spot clean/ replace of entrance mats and grates; floor strip/refinishing; sweep/vacuum and damp mop of flooring; vacuum (automatic type) pools; clean and disinfect pool deck; clean, damp mop and disinfect sauna room; cleaning and disinfect bathroom fixtures; waste removal; glass cleaning Other Tasks carpet/furniture shampooing and steam cleaning The approximate estimated cost for these services is $4,000,000.00 over two (2) years with the potential for three (3) additional one (1) year extensions and an increase in value up to $6,000,000.00. The estimated total potential value is approximately $10,000,000.00 over a possible five (5) year period. It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number:  SLSO2796 Title: Base Janitorial Services Total Potential Value: $10,000,000.00 Anticipated Posting: November 2026 Anticipated Contract Commencement: April 2027 Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a bidder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a bid for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential bidders with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number SLSO2796; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has  met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal or a bid DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP  to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Brad Jeaurond Coordinator, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada 204-765-3000, ext. 258-4094 Bradley.Jeaurond@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent or bidder agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the bidder or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated  sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: USZ Campus MITTE 1|2 / CVC 277.30 Salle Blanche
description: L'hôpital universitaire de Zurich (USZ) prévoit une rénovation complète de la zone centrale. Cette réorganisation a lieu au cours des opérations hospitalières en cours et est mis en œuvre en différentes étapes. Le projet Campus MITTE1|2 (CM1|2) constitue la première étape de la rénovation structurelle globale de l'USZ. Le projet comprend le démantèlement de plusieurs bâtiments, la construction d'un nouveau bâtiment MITTE 1|2 d'environ 44 mètres de haut et la rénovation/conversion de l'ancienne anatomie.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Zweiphasiger städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Wettbewerb nach RPW 2013 - Produktives Quartier Gutleut-West
description: Gegenstand des Wettbewerbes ist ein städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Entwurf in dem gezeigt wird, wie die Transformation eines gewerblich geprägten Bestandsareals zu einem nutzungsgemischten, klimaangepassten und gemeinwohlorientierten Quartier gelingen kann. In einer Stadt mit hoher Flächennachfrage und begrenzten innerstädtischen Entwicklungsreserven treffen hier Ansprüche unmittelbar aufeinander, die sich andernorts oft räumlich aus dem Weg gehen: Wohnen und Gewerbe, Logistik und Aufenthalt, soziale Infrastruktur und Produktion, Freiraum und Verdichtung. Die entscheidende Frage lautet deshalb nicht, welche Nutzung sich am Ende durchsetzt. Interessanter ist, wie aus dieser Konkurrenz ein Stück Stadt entstehen kann. Aufgabe des Wettbewerbs ist es, eine eigene räumliche Antwort zu entwickeln. Gesucht wird vornehmlich nicht das möglichst vollständige Bild eines irgendwann „fertigen“ Gutleut-West. Gesucht wird vielmehr ein städtebauliches und freiraumplanerisches Gerüst, das Orientierung gibt, ohne Entwicklung einzuschränken. Es soll durch zu entwickelnde Prinzipien Qualitäten sichern und zugleich Spielräume eröffnen – für unterschiedliche Nutzungen, Träger:innen, Eigentümer:innen und Entwicklungszeitpunkte. Die Ausloberin beabsichtigt, unter Würdigung der Empfehlung des Preisgerichts, das mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichnete Team mit der Ausarbeitung des Wettbewerbsergebnisses zu beauftragen. Die Ausloberin wird hierzu ein Verhandlungsverfahren ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb gemäß § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 VgV durchführen. Dabei behält sich die Ausloberin vor, das Verhandlungsverfahren zunächst nur mit dem mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichneten Team durchzuführen. Scheitern diese Verhandlungen oder besteht ein wichtiger Grund, der einer Beauftragung des 1. Preisträgers entgegensteht, werden die weiteren Preisträger zur Teilnahme an den Verhandlungen aufgefordert. Das Wettbewerbsergebnis wird im anschließenden Vergabeverfahren als Zuschlagskriterium mit 60 % gewichtet. Die Rangfolge der Preisträger gemäß der Entscheidung des Preisgerichts wird dabei entsprechend berücksichtigt, d.h. der 1. Preisträger erhält im Kriterium ‚Wettbewerbsergebnis' die höchste Punktzahl, der 2. Preisträger die zweithöchste usw. Die weitere Bearbeitung umfasst den städtebaulichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 51 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone IV, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie den freiräumlichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 52 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone IV, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie die Erstellung eines "Qualitätshandbuchs". Eine darüberhinausgehende Beauftragung weiterer Planungsleistungen bleibt vorbehalten und ist nicht Bestandteil dieses Auftragsversprechens. Ziel ist die Erarbeitung eines Rahmenplans mit integrierter Freiraumplanung als Vorstufe zum Bebauungsplan nach BauGB sowie als Grundlage für das im Anschluss geplante Konzeptverfahren für die hochbauliche Entwicklung auf den Baufeldern. Die Preisträger:innen verpflichten sich, im Falle einer Beauftragung durch die Ausloberin, die weitere Bearbeitung zu übernehmen und durchzuführen. Im Zuge der Überarbeitung der Wettbewerbsergebnisse treten sie mit der Bürgerschaft und Schlüsselpersonen vor Ort im Rahmen von Dialogformaten in Austausch (z.B. Vorstellung des Wettbewerbs-Ergebnisses, Rückfragenbeantwortung, Aufnahme von Hinweisen für weitere Bearbeitung). Die Beauftragung erfolgt vorbehaltlich des Abschlusses des erforderlichen Vergabeverfahrens, der erforderlichen haushaltsrechtlichen Voraussetzungen, der Eignung des Teilnehmers sowie des Vorliegens eines wichtigen Grundes, der einer Beauftragung entgegensteht. Im Falle einer weiteren Bearbeitung werden durch den Wettbewerb bereits erbrachte Leistungen des Preisträgers bis zur Höhe des zuerkannten Preises nicht erneut vergütet, wenn und soweit der Wettbewerbsentwurf unverändert der weiteren Bearbeitung zugrunde gelegt wird.

description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL or SOLICITATION AND DOES NOT COMMIT CMS TO AWARD A CONTRACT NOW OR IN THE FUTURE Introduction: This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is being issued to obtain capability statements from Small Businesses (SB)s that are capable, available and qualified to support Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), and specifically both the Center for Medicare (CM), Performance-based payment Policy Group (PPPG) and Office of Financial Management (OFM), Financial Services Group (FSG.) The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is hereby conducting market research to determine the availability and capability of potential small businesses (e.g., 8(a), service-disabled veteran owned small business, HUBZone small business, small disadvantaged business, veteran-owned small business and woman-owned small business) that can provide the services identified in the attached Accountable Care Organization Medicare Shared Savings Program Financial Services (ACO MSSP) draft Statement of Work (SOW), see Attachment 1. The purpose of this contract is to have a Contractor issue payments to Accountable Care Organizations (ACOs) participating in the Medicare Shared Savings Program (MSSP). The Contractor will perform financial services primarily to issue Electronic Funds Transfers to the ACOs, with additional support activities including validating payees, transaction monitoring and reconciliations and reporting. Contractors must be free of conflicts of interest or be able to prepare an Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) mitigation plan to address any actual, potential, or apparent organizational conflicts of interest that could arise. Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database located at https://www.sam.gov/ prior to award, during performance, and through final payment of any contract resulting from this Notice. Contractors may obtain information on SAM registration by visiting: https://www.acquisition.gov. This announcement is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) for planning purposes only. This is not an invitation for bid, request for quote or other solicitation and in no way obligates the Government to award a contract. CMS will not entertain questions regarding this market research. Background: The MSSP is a voluntary program that encourages groups of doctors, hospitals and other health care providers to come together as an ACO to give coordinated, high-quality care to their Medicare beneficiaries. When ACOs deliver on providing that care while improving patient health outcomes and reducing Medicare spending, they may be eligible to share in a portion of those savings. As of January 1, 2026, there are 511 ACOs participating in the MSSP servicing 12.6 million beneficiaries. Within the MSSP, CMS enters into agreements with ACOs. Within each performance year of the agreement period, the ACOs share in a percentage of the savings they generate if the expenditures of the ACO's assigned beneficiaries falls below the benchmark by an amount that meets or exceeds a minimum savings rate threshold, and if they also meet the quality performance standard and otherwise maintain their eligibility to participate in the MSSP. The MSSP also offers an Advance Investment Payment (AIP) option where eligible ACOs receive an upfront payment of $250,000 and two years of quarterly payments. The Center for Medicare (program office) is always evaluating the program performance and updating payment options, impacting the volume and frequency of payments to be disbursed to the ACOs. title: USAG Industrial Equipment Maintenance & Repair Services
description: The U.S. Government is seeking capable and responsible sources to provide non-personal services for the comprehensive maintenance, repair, inspection, and certification of cranes, hoists, scales, dock levelers, and vehicle lifts. The primary objective of these services is to ensure the continuous operational readiness, safety, and regulatory compliance of critical industrial lifting, weighing, and material handling equipment. Scope of Services The Contractor shall provide all necessary management, supervision, personnel, labor, equipment, tools, supplies, transportation, materials, and other items and services necessary to perform preventative maintenance, inspections, testing, calibrations, and emergency repairs for: Cranes & Hoists: Frequent and periodic inspections, preventative maintenance, and quadrennial load testing certified to 125% of rated capacity. Scales: Preventative maintenance, inspection, and calibration testing every six (6) months in accordance with NIST Handbook 44. Vehicle Lifts: Preventative maintenance and lift certification performed annually in accordance with ANSI/ALI ALOIMR2020 standards. Dock / Ramp Levelers & Trailer Restraints: Preventative maintenance, lubrication, repairs, and annual certifications. Unscheduled Repairs (Demand Maintenance Orders - DMOs): Responsive troubleshooting and repair services under strict timelines (Priority 1: Emergency within 24 hours, Priority 2: Urgent within 72 hours, Priority 3: Routine within 15 days). Locations Services will be performed at geographically dispersed locations at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. Supported sites include Pope Army Airfield (PAAF), Camp Mackall (MAAF), Simmons Army Airfield (SAAF), and Range Operations. Detailed Requirements All work shall be performed in accordance with the requirements and standards set forth in the Performance Work Statement (PWS) for this procurement, including compliance with Army TB 43-0142, 29 CFR 1910.179, and various ASME/ANSI standards. Contractor personnel must meet strict qualification standards, including five (5) years of maintenance experience for technicians and appropriate safety certifications (e.g., OSHA General Industry or Commercial Equivalent.) for the Project Manager. Contractor employees must be U.S. residents and successfully comply with all installation security requirements, including AT Level I, iWatch, OPSEC, and Threat Awareness (TARP) training. Interested parties should refer to the PWS for a complete understanding of the Government's needs.
